t: Funds made available under the heading “Medical services” in title II of division H of Public Law 112–74 may be used to carry out section 1787 of title 38, United States Code.

fable.w: This provision only authorizes previously appropriated funds to be used to carry out another statutory section. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: Funds made available under the heading “Medical services” in title II of division H of Public Law 112–74 may be used to carry out section 1787 of title 38, United States Code.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely administrative provision regarding the availability and use of appropriated funds. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or requirements to consult with states, tribes, or the public mentioned in this text.
qwen_block.s: Funds made available under the heading “Medical services” in title II of division H of Public Law 112–74 may be used to carry out section 1787 of title 38, United States Code.

opus.w: This provision only allows already-appropriated funds to be used for an existing statutory program. It does not require or allow any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or lawsuit involving anyone outside the federal government. The cross-reference to a benefits program is not participation, because the definition excludes benefits.
opus.s: Funds made available under the heading “Medical services” in title II of division H of Public Law 112–74 may be used to carry out section 1787 of title 38, United States Code.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** The tempting reading would be that citing section 1787 of title 38 (health care for family members of veterans who were at Camp Lejeune) brings in some outside process. It doesn't. This sentence only says certain appropriated funds may be spent on that program. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue. It is like Example 1, which was also just a statement about how funds may be used.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes the use of funds for medical services. It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in the decision-making process. The provision merely links funding to a specific statutory section regarding medical services, which falls under the exclusion for benefits/services rather than participation.
qwen_chat.s: Funds made available under the heading “Medical services” in title II of division H of Public Law 112–74 may be used to carry out section 1787 of title 38, United States Code.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "Medical services" implies interaction with patients (outsiders), but the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and providing services is not the same as consulting with outsiders before making a decision. The text is purely about the availability of funds for a specific statutory purpose.
